text:
- chief complaint: right elbow pain for about four days, worse on the inside of the elbow, with pain radiating into the forearm.
- history of present illness: the patient began pottery during the pandemic and developed medial elbow pain about a week ago, with no trauma or prior right elbow injury. Pain is rated 6/10, disrupts sleep, and limits lifting. Ibuprofen gives little relief.
- physical examination: vitals normal. Tenderness over the medial epicondyle. Pain with forearm pronation and with resisted wrist flexion. X-ray shows no fracture or bony abnormality.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: medial right elbow pain, forearm pain radiating down the arm, nighttime pain, difficulty lifting, pain with wrist and forearm movement.
- new medications prescribed or changed: ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours with food for one week.
- follow-up instructions: wear a sling while awake, apply ice to the elbow for 20 minutes three times a day, avoid pottery for the next couple of weeks, and return in one week for reassessment.
